passage:
Mentor note, written by Sunaina.
Lavanya, a junior designer in her second month, had been silent in every review. On Thursday the team lead closed her laptop and said, "Who sees a problem with this plan? I want the loudest disagreement in the room." Lavanya glanced at me. Then she said the navigation flow had too many steps. The lead answered, "Thank you, that changes the plan," and wrote it on the board.
After the meeting Lavanya told me, "I didn't know I was allowed." I suggested she notice how the lead reacts when someone disagrees. The following Monday she raised a second point unprompted, and the lead thanked her again.

qa.q: What did the team lead ask for at the Thursday review?
qa.a: The team lead asked for the loudest disagreement in the room.

qa.q: What did Lavanya feel when she said 'I didn't know I was allowed'?
qa.a: Lavanya felt relieved and a little surprised, realising that speaking up was welcome.

qa.q: What could Lavanya do to keep the good habit going?
qa.a: She could keep raising points with the lead, as she did on Monday, and watch how a good leader thanks the person who disagrees.

qa.q: Why might the team lead have said 'I want the loudest disagreement'?
qa.a: The lead may have wanted honest problems raised early and wanted quiet juniors to feel safe speaking, since the lead thanked Lavanya and changed the plan.

grounding: A junior watches a senior invite disagreement and thank the person who raised it, and feels safe to speak.

passage:
Tuesday. At planning, Nitin Sir asked, "Who disagrees with the Friday launch date?" Total silence. My mouth was dry, but I said the date was too tight for testing. Everyone looked at Nitin Sir, waiting for the frown. Instead he said, "Thank you. That is exactly what I needed to hear," and moved the launch to the following Tuesday. Then he wrote my name next to the point on the whiteboard.
My hands were still shaking in the corridor, but I felt safe, like a window had opened. Someone said his old team used to call him 'the door that is always open'. I think I know why. Next time I'll speak before he asks.
Nilesh

qa.q: What did Nitin Sir do with the launch date?
qa.a: He moved the launch to the following Tuesday.

qa.q: What was Nilesh feeling when speaking up and afterwards in the corridor?
qa.a: Nilesh was nervous, with a dry mouth and shaking hands, but also felt safe and relieved that the point was welcomed.

qa.q: What choice did Nilesh make at the meeting, and what might come next?
qa.a: Nilesh spoke about the tight date when nobody else did, and plans to speak before being asked next time.

qa.q: How might Nitin Sir see the person who disagrees with him?
qa.a: Nitin Sir seems to value them, since he thanked Nilesh, said it was what he needed to hear and wrote Nilesh's name by the point.

grounding: A junior watches a senior invite disagreement and thank the person who raised it, and feels safe to speak.
